question.text: An open cylindrical vessel filled with water is rotated together with water at angular speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. At this angular speed, the centre of the bottom is just exposed. If the angular speed is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, how much area (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>) of the bottom of the vessel is now exposed to surrounding? [Area of the cross-section of cylinder is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Let ω1 be initial angular velocity

ω12R22g=h
For angular velocity ω2 let radius of exposed surface be x

ω222gR2-x2=h
Putting the value of ω1 and ω2
πx2=9
Since πR2=27
